learning: Iteration 3 showed a shorter lookahead (y 0.04) cut the score from 454.6 to 131.9. The score rises with lookahead from y 0.04 to y 0.06, so this iteration tests y 0.07. The longer lookahead may add phase lag, which would show up as higher steering_oscillation.
notes: Iteration 1 controller kept unchanged on the Builder's y 0.07 geometry, so the race isolates the lookahead change. Watch steering_oscillation for phase lag from the longer lookahead.
rationale: Iteration 3 (y 0.04) scored 131.9, far below iteration 1 (y 0.06, 454.6). The oval finish rate fell from 18/20 to 0/20 and max_error rose to 0.065, so a shorter lookahead is clearly harmful. The Builder's candidate moves the sensors to y 0.07 on the iteration 1 geometry (16 mm footprints, x = ±0.024 m at 12 mm pitch, 0.12 m track, 0.8 kg). I am keeping the iteration 1 controller (kp 4.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.6, last_direction, weights [2,1,0,-1,-2]) and changing nothing else. The sensor x positions and weights are unchanged, so signal scale per unit error is the same as in iteration 1. Only the timing of the signal changes, so any difference is attributable to lookahead. Iteration 2 showed that changing the signal scale through span without retuning kp caused harm, so I am not retuning kp here. The main risk is phase lag from a longer lookahead, which could raise steering_oscillation (0.36 on the s-bend at y 0.06). The Builder's own feedback request asks whether this lag appears, so all measurements are requested to test it.
